title: Integrated Security & Compliance Controlbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This controlbook defines Redwood Inference's integrated security and compliance controls for role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC practices, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and management of risk and exceptions. It provides prescriptive controls, operational runbooks, ownership, and evidence requirements to support audits (SOC2, ISO27001) and enterprise customers.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood systems that process customer data (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployment management plane), developer/admin tooling, and the CI/CD pipeline. Non-applicable systems (e.g., public marketing websites) are explicitly exempted in Appendix A.

Table of contents:
1. RBAC & Authentication
2. Audit Logging
3. Data Residency & Retention
4. Secure SDLC
5. Incident Response (security-focused)
6. Compliance Evidence Workflows
7. Risk & Exceptions
8. Ownership & Contacts
9. Appendix: Control Mapping and Example Evidence

1) RBAC & Authentication

Intro: RBAC and strong authentication are primary controls to limit access to customer data and production systems. Our model is principle-of-least-privilege, role-scoped permissions, and just-in-time elevation for high-risk actions.

Standards:
- Identity provider: Okta (primary). Fallback: GCP Identity Platform for private deployments where Okta is unavailable.
- Authn: SAML 2.0 + OIDC for interactive access; service accounts use short-lived OAuth tokens or mTLS where required.
- MFA: Required for all interactive accounts with access to production. Enforced via Okta policy (factor: TOTP + security key preferred).
- Passwords: Organization-managed vaults; interactive passwords are discouraged (SSO-only preferred).

Roles and permission model:
- role:platform-admin -> full control over control plane, reserved for SRE/Platform leads. (Limit: <= 6 humans, require approval workflow).
- role:ops -> deploy, rollback, view SLO dashboards, view logs (anonymized).
- role:security -> audit, view raw logs, trigger incident response playbooks.
- role:developer -> deploy to non-prod, limited to dedicated namespaces in staging.
- role:customer-support -> view customer metadata and sanitized logs; cannot access PII or raw prompt/response content unless authorized.

Just-in-time access (JIT) process:
1. Request via internal access portal (ServiceNow/Concourse ticket).
2. Approver: owner of the resource or security on-call.
3. Duration: default 2 hours, max 8 hours.
4. All JIT elevations are logged and attached to ticket for evidence.

Separation of duties:
- No single engineer has both production access and billing/finance permissions.
- Infrastructure credential rotation is automated (see section 3.3 of infra-standards).

Example policy snippet (Okta group mapping):
- group:rbac-platform-admin -> role:platform-admin
- group:rbac-security -> role:security

2) Audit Logging

Objective: Maintain tamper-evident, centralized audit logs for authentication events, privileged access, administrative actions, configuration changes, and data access that support detection, forensics, and compliance evidence.

Logging scope and retention:
- Events captured: authentication (successful/failed), token issuance/revocation, role elevation/JIT, admin API calls (create/delete/update for models, routes, deployments), secret management actions (rotate/revoke), access to customer data (read/write), and incident actions.
- Log transport: all application and infra logs ship to centralized logging cluster (Elastic stack) and are replicated to immutable object store (GCS, EU/US region aligned with data residency policy).
- Retention default: 1 year for infra-auth and admin logs; 7 years for audit logs supporting regulated customers (configurable per contract).
- Integrity: logs are hashed and stored with daily signed manifests (SHA256) to detect tampering.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Log ingestion latency: >99% of events available in central index within 30s.
- Alerting: failed auth rate spike (>3x baseline or >50 failed attempts / minute) triggers P1 alert.

Access control for logs:
- Security team: read access to all raw logs.
- Platform admins: read/write to infra logs, read to application logs.
- Developer: anonymized view (PII/PHI redacted).

Audit runbook (for reviewers/auditors):
1. Verify daily signed manifest exists for date range.
2. Cross-check Okta audit events with internal admin API logs for changes to role assignments.
3. Provide sampled logs (redacted) and hash manifests as evidence.

Sample CLI to export signed manifest (example):
$ rcli audit export-manifest --from 2026-02-01 --to 2026-02-28 --output signed-manifests-2026-02.tar.gz

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy summary:
- Data residency is enforced per-customer configuration: options include US (multi-region us-central/us-east), EU (europe-west), APAC (asia-southeast).
- Control plane metadata may be stored centrally (US) unless customer requires full VPC/private on-prem installation.
- Customer-managed Private deployments: customer chooses region and retains primary control of storage.

Retention requirements (defaults and contract overrides):
| Data Type | Default Retention | Retention Purpose | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Authentication & admin logs | 1 year | Forensics and compliance | Extendable per contract to 7y |
| Request logs (metadata only) | 90 days | Billing, performance | Content-level logs redacted by default |
| Prompt & response content | 0 days (default) | Minimize risk | Persist only if customer opts in; retention configurable per contract |
| Embedding/Model outputs stored by customer | Per customer policy | N/A | Redwood does not default-store embeddings without opt-in |

Retention enforcement and deletion workflow:
1. Data deletion requested via support portal or automated TTL policies.
2. Deletion job runs in isolated job pool and writes deletion receipts to audit log.
3. Cryptographic erasure: keys are destroyed for encrypted blobs if supported, and manifests updated.

4) Secure SDLC

Objectives: Ensure security is built into the software development lifecycle through gated CI/CD, automated tests, static/dynamic scans, third-party dependency management, and release controls for production.

Mandatory controls:
- Pre-commit: developer linting and unit tests are required.
- CI pipeline controls:
  - SAST: run on every PR (Snyk + CodeQL).
  - Dependency scanning: block PRs with critical CVEs.
  - Secret scanning: fail build for detected secrets (trufflehog / Git guardian).
  - DAST: scheduled for main and release branches.
- Signing & provenance: release artifacts are signed with CI ephemeral keys; provenance recorded in artifact registry.
- Environment separation: production credentials are never injected into developer local environments; use ephemeral test credentials.

Release policy and rollouts:
1. Canary release (5% traffic) for 24 hours with automated rollback criteria (error rate > 2% increase or > 300 p95 latency ms increase).
2. Progressive rollout to 25%, 50%, 100% with 24h observation windows and automated rollback.

Developer checklist before merge:
1. PR has SAST/DAST scan results attached.
2. Unit and integration tests pass.
3. Threat model updated if the change affects authentication, storage, or network boundaries.
4. Release notes include data residency or retention changes if applicable.

5) Incident Response (security-focused)

Scope: Security incident response procedures for incidents affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer data or infra controls. This section complements the company incident response runbook in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response.

Detection & Triage:
- MTTD target: < 15 minutes for P1 security alerts (threat intel, IDS, anomalous admin actions).
- Initial triage owner: security on-call.

Containment & Eradication steps (high-level):
1. Isolate affected services (route to degraded capacity or remove admin access).
2. Rotate affected credentials and revoke tokens via centralized secrets manager.
3. Preserve forensic data: snapshot affected hosts, collect logs, lock daily signed manifest.
4. Engage legal and customer success for potential customer notifications.

Communication & SLA obligations:
- Internal: security postmortem within 72 hours (initial summary) and full timeline within 7 days.
- Customer: follow contractual notification timelines (typically within 72 hours for incidents involving customer data).

Forensics evidence checklist:
- Hashes of snapshots (SHA256).
- Copies of relevant audit logs and signed manifests.
- Chain-of-custody ticket numbers.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Goal: Provide reproducible evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits) with minimal manual effort.

Evidence categories & standard artifacts:
- Access control: Okta group membership snapshots, JIT tickets, RBAC policy exports.
- Logging: signed log manifests, sample redacted logs, ingestion and retention reports.
- SDLC: SAST/DAST scan reports, dependency scan baselines, release signatures and provenance.
- Incident response: postmortems, forensic hashes, notification logs.

Evidence collection process (auditor request):
1. Auditor submits request to compliance@redwood.ai with scope and time window.
2. Compliance owner (security-gov team) validates scope and issues access token for evidence bucket.
3. Automation job collects artifacts and bundles them to a read-only evidence bucket (GCS/S3) with manifest.
4. Provide redact scripts to scrub PII from sampled logs where required.

Retention of evidence packages: 7 years (by default) for audit artifacts unless contract specifies otherwise.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Risk acceptance process:
1. Team raises risk via risk register (Confluence page) with owner, description, compensating controls, and proposed duration.
2. Security reviews and assigns risk level (Low/Medium/High).
3. Risks rated High require Security Leadership and CTO approval and an automatic mitigation plan.

Temporary exceptions (e.g., onboarding a customer with unique residency need):
- Exception request must include business justification, technical plan, compensating controls, and an end date.
- Exceptions >30 days require quarterly review and sign-off by security and legal.

Monitoring compensating controls:
- Increase logging and monitoring scope for the exception window.
- Weekly exception status update in the security leadership meeting.

8) Ownership & Contacts

Primary owners:

9) Appendix: Control Mapping and Example Evidence

Control matrix (partial):
| Control | Evidence artifact | Owner | Retention |
|---|---|---|---:|
| RBAC group membership | Okta group snapshot CSV | Security | 3 years |
| JIT access tickets | Ticket export (ServiceNow) | Platform | 1 year |
| Audit log integrity | Signed manifest + hash | SRE | 7 years |
| SAST results | CodeQL report per PR | Eng-DevX | 1 year |

Example evidence manifest (text):
- manifest_id: MANIFEST-202602-01
- generated_by: automation-evidence-collector v1.4
- date_range: 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28
- artifacts: [okta-groups-202602.csv, signed-manifest-202602.tar.gz, codeql-summary-202602.json]
- verification: SHA256(manifest) = abcd1234...

Change history and governance:
- Major changes to this document must follow ADR process in /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records and be approved by Security Leadership.
- Annual review required; targeted cadence: Q4 each year or earlier when major policy changes occur.

How to use this document:
- Security engineers: use sections 1-3 for operational controls and runbooks.
- Compliance team: drive evidence requests through section 6 automation.
- Product and Sales: reference data residency and retention tables for customer contracts.

Contact for questions or exceptions: security@g.redwood.ai
